You are building **Track A (the work loop)** of the Co-learn prototype, in parallel with 4 other agents, each in its own git worktree. This is the critical path: real code execution streaming end-to-end.

## Read first
`CLAUDE.md`, `docs/design-plan.md` (esp. §2, §3, §5, §6, §9), `docs/product-vision.md`, `web/README.md`, `web/AGENTS.md`, and every file in `web/lib/contracts/`, plus `web/lib/claude/models.ts`, `web/lib/claude/client.ts`, `web/lib/engine/index.ts` (P0 stand-in; Track B is replacing it with the real engine with the same exports), `web/lib/claude/content/index.ts` (stand-in; Track D replacing), `web/lib/platform/limits.ts` (stand-in; Track E replacing), `web/lib/store/*`, `web/lib/views.ts`.

## Rules (all tracks)
- Work only in your owned paths: `web/app/api/chat/`, `web/lib/claude/work/`, `web/lib/client/` (new: browser-side stream helpers), `web/scripts/smoke-work.ts`. Do NOT edit `web/lib/contracts/*` (frozen), the stand-in files, or other tracks' paths. If a contract change is truly needed, work around it and describe it in your final report.
- Don't add npm dependencies (installed: @anthropic-ai/sdk 0.135, zod 4, @upstash/*, use-sound, motion, canvas-confetti, react-markdown, remark-gfm, vitest, jsdom, @testing-library/react). Setup: `cd web && npm ci`.
- Next.js 16: read `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` before using framework APIs (e.g., `cookies()` is async; `after()` from `next/server` exists for post-response work).
- If a `claude-api` skill is available via the Skill tool, invoke it before writing Claude calls and read `typescript/claude-api/tool-use.md` + `streaming.md` from it.
- Quality: strict TypeScript, small focused modules, comments only where non-obvious, match the existing code style. Vitest tests (`*.test.ts`) for all logic (mock the SDK stream).
- Before finishing: in `web/`, `npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run lint && npm run build` all pass.
- Commit on your worktree branch with clear messages ending with the line `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Don't push. Don't merge into main.
- Secrets: never print, log, or commit them. If `/Users/dinakar/Documents/coding/anthropic_take_home/web/.env.local` exists (Dinakar may add it during your run), you may copy it into your worktree's `web/.env.local` (gitignored) and make a SMALL number of live smoke calls (≤ 10 total). Never print its contents. If it doesn't exist, rely on mocked tests and leave `scripts/smoke-work.ts` runnable (`node --env-file=.env.local scripts/smoke-work.ts`; Node 24+ runs .ts via type stripping. Use only erasable TS syntax there).

## Claude API facts (verified, current)
- Work model: `MODELS.work` (claude-sonnet-5-5, effort "medium" via `output_config: { effort }`). **Omit `thinking`** (adaptive by default). Never send temperature/top_p, `thinking: {type:"disabled"}`, or assistant prefill (all 400). Forced `tool_choice` any/tool → 400: use auto, plus `strict: true` on our function tools (schema needs `additionalProperties: false` + `required`; zod 4 has `z.toJSONSchema`, but check the output is API-compatible and hand-write the JSON schema if not).
- Refusals: use the beta endpoint `anthropic().beta.messages.stream({... betas: ["server-side-fallback-2026-07-01"], fallbacks: "default" })`. Check `stop_reason === "refusal"` and emit a friendly error. Ignore `fallback` content blocks in the UI.
- Code execution: `CODE_EXECUTION_TOOL` = `{type:"code_execution_20260521", name:"code_execution"}`. Claude emits `server_tool_use` blocks named `bash_code_execution` (input `{command}`) or `text_editor_code_execution` (file create/view/str_replace). Results arrive as `bash_code_execution_tool_result` (content `{type:"bash_code_execution_result", stdout, stderr, return_code, content:[{type:"bash_code_execution_output", file_id}]}`) and `text_editor_code_execution_tool_result`. Map these to `code_start`/`code_result` events + `code_run` transcript items (language: python if the command runs python/heredoc python, else bash; file for text-editor ops). Collect output `file_id`s into `session.fileIds`.
- Container reuse: read `message.container?.id`, store as `session.containerId`, and pass `container: id` on every later request. If a request fails because the container is expired or invalid (a 400 mentioning container), retry once without it. Emit a `notice` ("The coding environment was reset; reloading data.") and tell Claude in the user turn to reload data from the uploaded files.
- `stop_reason === "pause_turn"`: append the assistant content and re-send (count toward the step cap). Cap the loop at 8 model requests per turn → `turn_end` reason `max_steps`.
- Demo data: on the first turn of a session with `intent.demo === true` and `process.env.DEMO_FILE_ID` set (and `session.demoFileAttached` false), add `{type:"container_upload", file_id}` to the user content and set `demoFileAttached`. If DEMO_FILE_ID is missing, tell Claude to generate a realistic synthetic churn dataset in the sandbox instead (~5,000 rows, ~15% churn, a leaky `cancellation_request_date` column, a few missing `total_charges`).
- **Preserved thinking: history must be append-only.** Store and resend assistant `content` exactly as returned (including thinking blocks). Never edit or delete earlier messages (newer accounts get a 400 on edited history). So NO custom compaction that rewrites history (10-min sessions won't approach the 1M context).
- Mid-conversation system messages are supported on Sonnet 5.5: `{role:"system", content}` inside `messages[]`. It must follow a user message and be last, or be followed by an assistant turn; it can't be first. Use one per turn, appended right after that turn's user message, for the **dynamic context** (engine summary, time remaining, sketch). Keep them in history (append-only).
- Prompt caching: stable, deterministic `tools` and `system` (put `cache_control: {type:"ephemeral"}` on the last system block) so the prefix caches. Nothing volatile (timestamps, IDs) in the system prompt.
- Errors: typed `Anthropic.APIError` subclasses. Call `checkLimits(anonId, ip)` before the turn (emit an `error` event with code `rate_limited` or `spend_cap` and stop if not ok). Call `recordUsage(anonId, ip, model, usage)` after every model response.

## What to build
1. **`POST /api/chat`** (`app/api/chat/route.ts`, `export const runtime = "nodejs"`, `export const maxDuration = 300`). Body: `ChatRequest`. Identify the user with `readAnonId()` (401 if missing); load the session and check `session.anonId` matches (404 otherwise). Respond with a streaming `Response` of NDJSON `ChatStreamEvent`s (`Content-Type: application/x-ndjson`). Request kinds:
   - `message`: the user's text (≤ 4,000 chars; 400 otherwise). If a moment is pending (`session.engine.pendingMomentId`), mark that moment `skipped`, clear pending, and prefix the user text for Claude with a short note that the learner skipped it.
   - `moment_response`: the server builds the user text from the stored `MomentRecord` (never trust client text):
     - Answered: the answer, verdict, and why.
     - Skipped or deferred: "Learner skipped/deferred; make the call yourself and briefly say why."
     - Predict moments (status `awaiting_prediction_result`): "The learner predicted: X. Now run the code, then call resolve_prediction with moment_id=…".
     - Always end with "Continue the work, building on their choice."
   - `boss_result`: the text comes from the `BossState` outcome plus concepts.
   - `continue`: resume.
2. **Work loop** (`lib/claude/work/loop.ts` and friends), a manual streaming loop with the native SDK. Tools: code execution plus three strict function tools whose `input_schema` matches `LearningMomentInputSchema`, `ResolvePredictionInputSchema`, and `MilestoneInputSchema` (validate every tool input with zod; on failure, return an `is_error` tool_result). Behaviour per tool:
   - **`learning_moment`**:
     1. Create a `MomentRecord` and run `engine.gate(candidate, ctx)`. Build `ctx` from `session.engine`, `store.getMastery(anonId)`, `user.settings`, `intent.familiarity`, and now. Log `moment_proposed` / `moment_gated` events.
     2. If shown, call `content.verifyMoment`. If not ok, treat as skip `unverified`.
     3. **Skip/defer:** return tool_result `{status:"skip", reason}` and keep looping in the same request (defer: store the moment with status `deferred` for the wrap-up quiz).
     4. **Show:** save the moment (status `awaiting_answer`), update the engine with `engine.recordShown`, emit a `moment` event with `toMomentView`, append the tool_result `{status:"awaiting_learner", moment_id}` to history, and END the turn with `turn_end` reason `awaiting_learner`.
   - **`resolve_prediction`**: load the moment (status `awaiting_prediction_result`). Set the verdict and why, mark it `answered`, award XP via `engine.xpFor({kind:"prediction", verdict})`, and update `user.xp` (use `engine.levelFor` before and after for `levelUp`, and add rewards from `engine.rewardsBetween` to `user.unlocks`). Update mastery with `engine.updateMastery` and `store.putMastery`, and the outcome with `engine.recordOutcome`. Emit `prediction_reveal` with an `XpAward`, then tool_result "recorded", and continue.
   - **`milestone_reached`**: compute `engine.bossDue(session.engine, now, sessionEndsAt)`. Emit `milestone`. If due, return tool_result `{boss_due:true, instruction:"Stop here and wait: a short boss challenge starts now. Don't continue the work until its result arrives."}` and end the turn with reason `boss_due`. Otherwise return `{boss_due:false}` and continue.
   - Call `engine.recordWorkTurn` once per user turn.
   - Status events: `thinking` at the start, `running_code` when a server_tool_use starts, `preparing_moment` while gating/verifying.
3. **System prompt** (`lib/claude/work/prompt.ts`): Co-learn rules from the design plan:
   - Work first: do the user's task well, concisely.
   - When a genuinely valuable learning opportunity arises in the flow of work, call `learning_moment` INSTEAD of continuing. Never answer your own question; the turn pauses for the learner.
   - The moment-type guide and the learning-value scale (5/4/3/2/1 as in §6.2). Be honest; most turns have no moment.
   - Predict moments come before running the code that reveals the answer; afterwards call `resolve_prediction` comparing against the real output.
   - Decide moments: build on the learner's choice. Learning by consequence: if the choice is weak but safe, follow it, let the real results show the effect, then offer to switch; if costly, explain and ask them to reconsider.
   - Keep moments small (one question answerable in 1–3 sentences; concept card ≤ 60 words on first exposure).
   - Code-execution guidance: small steps, concise prints, save charts to PNG files (matplotlib, `savefig`), reload data from files each turn (variables may not persist).
   - Call `milestone_reached` when a meaningful chunk of work completes (e.g., data explored, first model trained, model improved).
   - Style: friendly, concise markdown, no lectures.
4. **Context assembly** (`lib/claude/work/context.ts`): the dynamic context text from `engine.summarize(ctx)` plus remaining minutes (from `session.createdAt` + `intent.minutes`; at ≥ 80% elapsed, say "~2 minutes left: steer toward a milestone"), plus the sketch (milestones, concept radar) if present. Rendered as the mid-conversation system message for that turn.
5. **Persistence**: append-only `ApiMessages` via `store.put/getApiMessages`, transcript items, moments, and user XP.
   - **Race safety:** other routes (Track D) patch `session.sketch`/`title`/`story` in the background. So right before every `putSession`, re-read the latest session and apply only the fields you own (`engine`, `containerId`, `fileIds`, `demoFileAttached`). Persist at moment/turn boundaries and in a `finally` on errors.
6. **Browser helper** (`lib/client/chatStream.ts`): `streamChat(req: ChatRequest, onEvent, signal)`. It POSTs, parses NDJSON robustly (partial lines across chunks), calls `onEvent` per `ChatStreamEvent`, and resolves on stream end. Include a pure `parseNdjsonChunks` with tests. Also a pure reducer, `applyEvent(items: TranscriptItem[], event)`, so the UI can build transcript state from events (text deltas append to the matching `assistant_text` item; code_start/code_result update the `code_run` item; moment/prediction_reveal/milestone/notice add items). Test it.
7. **Smoke script** `scripts/smoke-work.ts`: creates a session in-process (MemoryStore) or calls the route directly, sends "Load the churn data and tell me the churn rate", and prints the event types. If you have the key, run it and fix issues (verify code execution, container reuse across two turns, and that a learning_moment can be proposed). Note: Track D generates the real dataset. For your live test, upload a tiny CSV yourself via `anthropic().files.upload` (check the SDK's files resource types; out of beta) or let Claude synthesize data.

## Final report (≤ 400 words)
What you built (files), tests, how P2 integration should use it (route + client helper + reducer), live-test results (or that none were possible), known gaps/TODOs, contract change requests, your branch name, and final commit hash.

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

Reach for this when the task matches an available agent type, when you have independent work to run in parallel, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate it and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps. For a single-fact lookup where you already know the file, symbol, or value, search directly. Once you've delegated a search, don't also run it yourself — wait for the result.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

# CLAUDE.md — project context for Claude Code

## What this is
Dinakar's take-home for the **Full Stack Engineer, Education Labs** role at Anthropic.
Build a deployed prototype (using the Claude API) that enhances human learning and agency,
plus a written design rationale and a ≤8-minute video. Full brief: `docs/assignment-brief.md`.

Official deadline: **Oct 21, 2026, 9:00 AM PT**. Personal target: Oct 20. Expected effort: < 1 day; depth over breadth.

## Working agreements (important)
- **Dinakar owns the design decisions.** The evaluators assess *his* judgment in guiding Claude,
  not Claude's raw output. When a design choice comes up, present options with trade-offs and a
  recommendation — don't silently decide. Ask for his reasoning when it isn't stated.
- **Log decisions.** When Dinakar makes a meaningful design/technical decision, append it to
  `docs/decision-log.md` (date, decision, alternatives considered, his rationale).
- **Never commit secrets.** API keys live in `.env` (gitignored). Use `.env.example` for placeholders.
- Only commit/push when asked.
- Prefer simple and thoughtful over complex. Pick one specific user journey and go deep.

## Direction (2026-10-17)
Option B: **Co-learn**, a Claude mode where users do real work with Claude and get short, game-like learning moments
triggered by their work. Demo: a working professional training an ML model. See `docs/product-vision.md`.

- `docs/design-plan.md` — **build blueprint** (architecture, tools, engine, data model, build order)

- `docs/context-persistence.md` — storage and model-context plan
- `reference/research/` — research reports; `reference/ascii-characters.md` — character art
- `alternative-projects/` — archived ideas, not part of the submission

- App lives in `web/` (Next.js 16; read `web/AGENTS.md` and `web/README.md` first).
- Shared contracts in `web/lib/contracts/` are frozen during parallel tracks; propose changes instead of silently editing.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

content.content:
# Co-learn: detailed design plan (v1)

Drafted by Claude with Dinakar, 2026-10-17. This is the build blueprint. It implements the decisions in
`docs/product-vision.md`, `docs/design-principles.md`, `docs/context-persistence.md`, and `docs/decision-log.md`.
Items marked **(proposed)** are new design choices made in this plan and need Dinakar's sign-off (see §17).

---

## 1. What we're building

**Co-learn** is a mode for Claude where a working professional does real work with Claude and comes out more capable.
Claude collaborates on the task normally, including running real code. At high-value moments it pauses and turns the
work into a short challenge the user solves themselves. The user's answer then steers the work.

**The one user journey we optimize for (demo + video):** a professional who knows some Python but is new to ML trains a
churn-prediction model on a CSV with Claude, in about 10 minutes, and leaves understanding class imbalance, metric
choice, data leakage, and overfitting, because they made those calls themselves.

**Generality:** any task works (writing, SQL, analysis, planning). The churn demo is a one-click starter, not a constraint.

### Success criteria for the prototype
1. A reviewer can open the URL, type `/co-learn`, click "Try the demo", and finish a full session (moments → boss → wrap-up) in ~10 minutes with no setup.
2. Code runs for real: real metrics, real charts.
3. Learning moments feel *earned by the work*, not bolted on. The user's answers visibly change what Claude does.
4. Nothing feels punishing or cluttered.

---

## 2. Experience walkthrough (the demo journey)

| # | Screen / moment | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | **Unlock** | A centered input with `/co-learn` as placeholder; caption: "Type /co-learn to switch on Co-learn mode." Typing it plays an unlock chime and the box "opens". The server sets the anonymous ID cookie. |
| 1 | **Intent** | Pip (ASCII robot) asks: "What are you working on?" A free-text box plus one chip: **▶ Try the demo: train a churn model**. Then two quick chip questions: familiarity (*New to this / Some experience / Comfortable*) and time (*10 min* default / 20 / 30). |
| 2 | **Work starts immediately** | Claude loads the CSV in the sandbox and shows its shape and churn rate (~15%) as **real output**. The session sketch is generated in the background and doesn't block. |
| 3 | **Predict moment** | Before Claude trains anything: "If a model predicts *nobody* churns, what accuracy would it get?" User: "about 85%". ✓ Correct; chime; +10 XP; Pip happy. The why: "Accuracy rewards the majority class, so it can look great while missing every churner." |
| 4 | **Decide moment** | "Missing a churner costs more than a false alarm. Which metric should we optimize: accuracy, precision, recall, or F1?" User picks recall (or anything defensible). **Claude builds the pipeline around their choice.** If the choice is weak but safe (e.g., accuracy), Claude follows it and lets the real results show the consequence, then offers to switch: learning by consequence. |
| 5 | **Spot-the-issue moment** | Claude shows the feature list: "One of these columns would make the model look amazing but fail in production. Which, and why?" (The planted leak: `cancellation_request_date`.) Free-form answer; if the user misses it → multiple choice → feedback. |
| 6 | **Real training** | Claude trains (e.g., logistic regression vs. gradient boosting), shows real precision/recall and a confusion-matrix chart. |
| 7 | **Milestone → boss** | "First model trained" milestone. **Boss: The Overfit Bug** (ASCII + HP bar). 2–3 linked questions recombining the session's concepts, e.g., "Train recall 0.98, test recall 0.52. What's happening, and what's your first fix?" Each good answer hits the boss. Victory → jingle → **story chapter** unlocks. |
| 8 | **Wrap-up** (at ~10 min, offered, never forced) | Deferred-quiz items (if any) → **Codex** (concepts learned, with how you did) → XP total, **level-up** → unlock toast ("New theme: Sunset") → "Next time you could…" suggestions. |

---

## 3. Key design choices (and why)

1. **Learning moments are a tool Claude calls** **(proposed)**. Claude gets a `learning_moment` tool. When it sees a good
   opportunity *in the flow of the work*, it calls the tool instead of continuing. This is how "work first, inject learning"
   becomes concrete:

- **Stack:** Next.js 16 (App Router) + TypeScript + Tailwind v4. **Native `@anthropic-ai/sdk`** for all Claude calls

  plus the session ID, and the server assembles context. This makes resume, compaction, and caps straightforward.

---

## 5. The work turn: how the loop actually runs

### 5.1 Tools available to the work model
| Tool | Kind | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `code_execution` | Anthropic server tool (`codeExecution_20260120` via AI SDK) | Run Python in the sandbox: load data, train, plot |
| `learning_moment` | Our function tool; `execute` runs the gate | Propose a learning moment (schema in §6) |
| `resolve_prediction` | Our function tool; `execute` records the result | After running code, reveal how the user's prediction compared to the real result |
| `milestone_reached` | Our function tool; `execute` checks whether a boss is due | Mark the end of a work chunk ("data explored", "first model trained") |

### 5.2 Sequence
```
user message ──▶ /api/chat
  1. rate-limit + spend-cap check
  2. load session, history, engine state, mastery → assemble context (§9)
  3. streamText(Sonnet 5.5, effort medium, tools, container id, stopWhen = awaitingLearner OR stepCount ≥ 8)
       ├─ Claude streams text, runs code (results stream to UI)
       ├─ Claude calls learning_moment(candidate)
       │     execute → engine.gate(candidate, state, settings)
       │        ├─ rejected  → returns {status:"skip", reason}  → Claude keeps working (same request)
       │        └─ accepted  → verify (Haiku, ~1s, §8) → returns {status:"awaiting_learner", momentId}
       │                         → stopWhen fires → stream ends → UI renders MomentCard
       ├─ Claude calls resolve_prediction(...) → UI renders PredictionReveal (+XP)
       └─ Claude calls milestone_reached(...) → engine: bossDue? → {boss_due:true} → stream ends → UI calls /api/boss
  4. onFinish: persist messages, container id, chart file ids, token usage (spend cap), events
```

### 5.3 After the learner answers
```
answer ──▶ /api/moment/grade (Haiku, structured) ──▶ UI: verdict + why + XP + sound + Pip reaction
                                                 └─▶ immediately POST /api/chat with a "moment response" message:
   "Learner response to moment m3 (decide · class imbalance): '<answer>'. Grade: correct. Why: …
    Continue the work, building on their choice."      (skip/defer: "Learner skipped; make the call yourself, briefly say why.")
```

### 5.4 Edge cases
- **`pause_turn`** (the sandbox hit its 10-step limit): the AI SDK reports it as a normal stop. Detect "ended right after a code
  result with no text" and auto-continue once. The prompt also asks Claude to keep code steps small.
- **Container expired or invalid:** retry without the container ID, re-attach the dataset, and tell Claude "The environment was
  reset; reload the data from /files."
- **Refusal** (`stop_reason: "refusal"`): show a friendly message and offer to rephrase.
- **Model error or timeout:** a retry button, and the message stays in the input.

## 6. Learning moments: the contract

### 6.1 `learning_moment` tool input (structured, strict)
```ts
{
  type: "decide" | "predict" | "explain_back" | "spot_issue" | "fill_gap",
  concept: string,              // short canonical name, e.g. "class imbalance" (used for mastery)
  concept_card?: string,        // ≤ 60 words; include on first exposure
  question: string,             // one clear question, answerable in 1–3 sentences
  ideal_answer: string,
  rubric: { key_points: string[]; acceptable_variants?: string[]; misconceptions?: string[] },
  mc_fallback: { options: string[] /* 3–4 */; correct_index: number; why: string[] /* one per option */ },
  difficulty: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5,
  first_exposure: boolean,
  learning_value: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5,
  value_reason: string,         // one line: why this matters for *this* user's goal
  costly_mistake: boolean,      // true if the user is about to make a choice with real consequences
  timing: "before_step" | "after_step"
}
```
- **Decide** moments may have several defensible answers. The rubric grades the *reasoning*, and `correct_index` marks the best option.
- **Predict** moments have `timing: "before_step"`. Their final grading comes from `resolve_prediction` after the real run.

### 6.2 Learning-value scale (in the system prompt)
| Score | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 5 | A real fork in *their* work, or a core concept they need for their goal right now |
| 4 | An important concept that's new to them and just came up |
| 3 | Useful but tangential |
| 2 | Trivia |
| 1 | Noise |

### 6.3 MomentCard states
`question` → (submit | **Show options** | **Skip** | **Quiz me later**) → `grading` (~1s) → `feedback`.
- **Feedback** shows a verdict chip ("Nice!" / "Partly" / "Not quite"), the why, an XP chip, and Pip's reaction.
- **Not quite / struggling** → "Try with options" (MC, graded in code) → feedback.
- **Partial** → feedback names what's missing (0.5 credit, no retry loop).
- Every card has a small "⚑ Report question" link (P9).

---

## 7. Pacing engine (pure TypeScript, unit-tested; `lib/engine/`)

### 7.1 Gate
```
gate(candidate, state, settings) → show | skip(reason) | defer
  if state.pendingMoment                                        → skip("one at a time")
  if candidate.learning_value < threshold(settings)
     and not breakthrough(candidate)                            → skip("low value")
  if isMastered(candidate.concept) and not reviewDue(concept)   → skip("mastered")
  if |candidate.difficulty − targetDifficulty(concept, type)| ≥ 2 → skip("off band")
  if settings.guardrails.enabled and capsExceeded(state, mode)
     and not breakthrough(candidate)                            → mode == strict ? defer : skip("cap")
  → show
breakthrough(c) = c.costly_mistake and c.learning_value == 5
```

### 7.2 Thresholds and guardrails (initial values, tuned via tests and play)
| Mode | Value threshold | Caps (soft) |
|---|---|---|
| **Off (default)** | ≥ 4 | none |
| Light | ≥ 4 | ≥ 1 work turn between moments |
| Balanced | ≥ 4 | ≤ 4 per 10 min; ≥ 2 turns between |
| Strict (fewest interruptions) | 5 only | ≤ 2 per 10 min; the rest deferred to the wrap-up quiz |

### 7.3 Mastery and difficulty (Elo-lite, P5)
- Per concept: θ (starts from familiarity: *new* 1.5, *some* 2.5, *comfortable* 3.5), attempt count n, lastSeen.
- P(correct) = σ(1.2·(θ − b)), where b is the question's difficulty (1–5).
- Update: θ += K·(score − p), with K = 0.6 while n < 3, then 0.3. Score: correct 1, partial 0.5, correct after MC 0.6, incorrect 0, skipped (no update).
- **Target success rate:** 0.87 for first exposure · 0.80 for practice · 0.72 for boss → target b = θ − logit(target)/1.2, clamped to 1–5.
- **Rolling adjustment:** over the last 5 graded moments, ≥ 90% correct → target b + 0.5 (ramp up gently); ≤ 60% → target b − 1 (back off fast).
- **Mastered:** n ≥ 2 and P(correct at b = 3) ≥ 0.8. **Review due** (P1, cross-session): mastered concept not seen for more than 1 day.
- The engine tells Claude the target difficulty and the mastered concepts *in advance* (dynamic context, §9), so most candidates already pass the gate. The gate is the backstop.

### 7.4 Bosses
- `milestone_reached` → boss due if: ≥ 3 distinct concepts have been practised since the last boss **and** no boss in the last 3 minutes **and** time remains.
- **Boss** = 2–3 linked questions with an HP bar. A hit for each correct answer (half a hit for partial).
- **Outcomes:** *flawless* / *victory* / *the bug retreats* (fewer than half the hits). All outcomes give XP and continue the story. Concepts from a retreat go to review.

### 7.5 Session clock
- At 80% of the session length, the engine tells Claude: "~2 minutes left: steer toward a milestone."
- At 100%, the UI offers **Wrap up** or **Keep going** (P7: never forced).

---

## 8. Trustworthy content (P9)
- **Verification** (accepted moments only, Haiku, ~1s): the verifier answers the question without seeing the key. Then it checks
  that the key and the MC `correct_index` agree, and flags ambiguity. If they disagree or it's ambiguous, the gate converts the
  decision to skip, so Claude simply keeps working.
- **Predict** moments are checked against real code output.
- **Report button** logs a `moment_reported` event and excludes that moment from XP and mastery.
- **Grader:** Haiku with the rubric + ideal answer + misconceptions. Structured output: `{verdict, why, missing_points[], misconception?}`.
  If testing shows mis-grades, switch grading to Sonnet (a config change).

---

## 9. Context assembly and models

### 9.1 What the work model sees each turn
| Block | Contents | Caching |
|---|---|---|
| System | Co-learn rules (work first; propose moments via the tool; value scale; never answer your own question; build on the learner's choices; learning by consequence; keep moments small), moment-type guidance, code-execution guidance (small steps, concise prints, save charts as PNG, reload data from files), style | Cached |
| Session | Intent (goal, familiarity, time), session sketch (milestones, concept radar) once ready | Cached once present |
| Dynamic | Elapsed/remaining time, guardrail mode, target difficulty, mastered concepts, concepts practised since the last boss, last 3 moment outcomes, rolling summary | Not cached |
| Messages | The last ~12 messages verbatim; older turns compacted into the rolling summary (Haiku) when over ~40K tokens | — |

### 9.2 Model routing
| Call | Model | Effort | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| Session sketch (milestones, concept radar, novice flag) | Opus 5.5 | high | structured |
| Work turn | Sonnet 5.5 (Opus 5.5 fallback via config) | medium | stream + tools |
| Boss generation | Sonnet 5.5 | high | structured |
| Story bible + chapters | Sonnet 5.5 | medium | structured |
| Wrap-up (codex + suggestions) | Sonnet 5.5 | medium | structured |
| Moment verification, grading, compaction | Haiku 5.5 | low/default | structured |

All model IDs and effort levels live in one config file (`lib/claude/models.ts`), which is also the seam for model-agnosticism (P1).
Exact `effort` and thinking parameter support per model is to be verified against the docs at build time.

### 9.3 Estimated cost per 10-minute demo session
| Item | Estimate |
|---|---|
| ~10 work turns on Sonnet (mostly cached input) | $0.25–0.50 |
| Opus sketch | ~$0.07 |
| Boss + story + wrap-up | ~$0.10 |
| Haiku calls | ~$0.01 |
| Sandbox time | Within the free 1,550 container-hours a month |
| **Total** | **≈ $0.40–0.70** |

## 1. What we're building

**Co-learn** is a mode for Claude where a working professional does real work with Claude and comes out more capable.
Claude collaborates on the task normally, including running real code. At high-value moments it pauses and turns the
work into a short challenge the user solves themselves. The user's answer then steers the work.

churn-prediction model on a CSV with Claude, in about 10 minutes, and leaves understanding class imbalance, metric
choice, data leakage, and overfitting, because they made those calls themselves.

```
breakthrough(c) = c.costly_mistake and c.learning_value == 5
```

### 7.2 Thresholds and guardrails (initial values, tuned via tests and play)
| Mode | Value threshold | Caps (soft) |
|---|---|---|
| **Off (default)** | ≥ 4 | none |
| Light | ≥ 4 | ≥ 1 work turn between moments |
| Balanced | ≥ 4 | ≤ 4 per 10 min; ≥ 2 turns between |
| Strict (fewest interruptions) | 5 only | ≤ 2 per 10 min; the rest deferred to the wrap-up quiz |

### 7.3 Mastery and difficulty (Elo-lite, P5)
- Per concept: θ (starts from familiarity: *new* 1.5, *some* 2.5, *comfortable* 3.5), attempt count n, lastSeen.
- P(correct) = σ(1.2·(θ − b)), where b is the question's difficulty (1–5).
- Update: θ += K·(score − p), with K = 0.6 while n < 3, then 0.3. Score: correct 1, partial 0.5, correct after MC 0.6, incorrect 0, skipped (no update).
- **Target success rate:** 0.87 for first exposure · 0.80 for practice · 0.72 for boss → target b = θ − logit(target)/1.2, clamped to 1–5.
- **Rolling adjustment:** over the last 5 graded moments, ≥ 90% correct → target b + 0.5 (ramp up gently); ≤ 60% → target b − 1 (back off fast).
- **Mastered:** n ≥ 2 and P(correct at b = 3) ≥ 0.8. **Review due** (P1, cross-session): mastered concept not seen for more than 1 day.
- The engine tells Claude the target difficulty and the mastered concepts *in advance* (dynamic context, §9), so most candidates already pass the gate. The gate is the backstop.

### 7.4 Bosses
- `milestone_reached` → boss due if: ≥ 3 distinct concepts have been practised since the last boss **and** no boss in the last 3 minutes **and** time remains.
- **Boss** = 2–3 linked questions with an HP bar. A hit for each correct answer (half a hit for partial).
- **Outcomes:** *flawless* / *victory* / *the bug retreats* (fewer than half the hits). All outcomes give XP and continue the story. Concepts from a retreat go to review.

### 7.5 Session clock
- At 80% of the session length, the engine tells Claude: "~2 minutes left: steer toward a milestone."
- At 100%, the UI offers **Wrap up** or **Keep going** (P7: never forced).

---

## 8. Trustworthy content (P9)
- **Verification** (accepted moments only, Haiku, ~1s): the verifier answers the question without seeing the key. Then it checks
  that the key and the MC `correct_index` agree, and flags ambiguity. If they disagree or it's ambiguous, the gate converts the
  decision to skip, so Claude simply keeps working.
- **Predict** moments are checked against real code output.
- **Report button** logs a `moment_reported` event and excludes that moment from XP and mastery.
- **Grader:** Haiku with the rubric + ideal answer + misconceptions. Structured output: `{verdict, why, missing_points[], misconception?}`.
  If testing shows mis-grades, switch grading to Sonnet (a config change).

---

## 9. Context assembly and models

### 9.1 What the work model sees each turn
| Block | Contents | Caching |
|---|---|---|
| System | Co-learn rules (work first; propose moments via the tool; value scale; never answer your own question; build on the learner's choices; learning by consequence; keep moments small), moment-type guidance, code-execution guidance (small steps, concise prints, save charts as PNG, reload data from files), style | Cached |
| Session | Intent (goal, familiarity, time), session sketch (milestones, concept radar) once ready | Cached once present |
| Dynamic | Elapsed/remaining time, guardrail mode, target difficulty, mastered concepts, concepts practised since the last boss, last 3 moment outcomes, rolling summary | Not cached |
| Messages | The last ~12 messages verbatim; older turns compacted into the rolling summary (Haiku) when over ~40K tokens | — |

### 9.2 Model routing
| Call | Model | Effort | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| Session sketch (milestones, concept radar, novice flag) | Opus 5.5 | high | structured |
| Work turn | Sonnet 5.5 (Opus 5.5 fallback via config) | medium | stream + tools |
| Boss generation | Sonnet 5.5 | high | structured |
| Story bible + chapters | Sonnet 5.5 | medium | structured |
| Wrap-up (codex + suggestions) | Sonnet 5.5 | medium | structured |
| Moment verification, grading, compaction | Haiku 5.5 | low/default | structured |

All model IDs and effort levels live in one config file (`lib/claude/models.ts`), which is also the seam for model-agnosticism (P1).
Exact `effort` and thinking parameter support per model is to be verified against the docs at build time.

### 9.3 Estimated cost per 10-minute demo session
| Item | Estimate |
|---|---|
| ~10 work turns on Sonnet (mostly cached input) | $0.25–0.50 |
| Opus sketch | ~$0.07 |
| Boss + story + wrap-up | ~$0.10 |
| Haiku calls | ~$0.01 |
| Sandbox time | Within the free 1,550 container-hours a month |
| **Total** | **≈ $0.40–0.70** |

**Size and balance:** 5,000 rows, ~15% churn.

# Product vision: Co-learn (v1, Option B)

Authored with Dinakar, 2026-10-17. The previous topic-to-game vision is archived in `alternative-projects/learning-quest/`.

## One-liner
**Co-learn is a mode for Claude where you get real work done *and* come out more capable.** Claude collaborates on
your task as usual, but at the right moments it turns the work into short, game-like challenges you solve yourself.
Your answers often steer the work.

## Framing
Imagined as a mode that ships inside Claude (e.g., `/co-learn` in Claude.ai or Claude Code). The prototype is a
standalone web app that emulates that mode on the Claude API.

## Target user and demo
- **User:** a working professional using Claude to get a task done in an area where they're not yet an expert, who wants to grow rather than just delegate.
- **Demo scenario (video):** training a machine-learning model, e.g., "help me train a model to predict customer churn from this CSV".
- **Session length:** 10 minutes by default.

## Experience
0. **Unlock.** The landing page is a single input whose placeholder shows `/co-learn` like a password hint. Typing it
   unlocks the site with a small animation and sound. It frames Co-learn as a mode you switch on. It is **not**
   security: the "password" is shown on screen, so abuse protection comes from rate limits.
1. **Intent.** At most 2–3 quick questions: what are you working on, how familiar are you with this area, and roughly
   how long you have (10 minutes by default). Learning guardrails are off by default (see Pacing).
2. **Work.** The user prompts and Claude works on the task, as in normal Claude.
3. **Learning moments.** Small, discrete challenges triggered by what the user is doing *right now*, not a pre-planned
   curriculum (the work changes too much as it goes). Each moment:
   - an optional 2–4 sentence concept card,
   - a free-form question,
   - a multiple-choice version if the user struggles,
   - a short "why" as feedback, plus XP and a sound,
   - then Claude continues the work, using the user's answer where it applies.
4. **Milestone bosses.** When a chunk of work completes (data prepared, first model trained), a short boss challenge
   recombines the concepts from recent moments, e.g., "Train accuracy is 99% and validation is 61%. What's happening, and what's the first thing you'd change?"
5. **Wrap-up.** A recap "codex" of concepts learned this session, XP and level progress, a story chapter (a surprise,
   lightly themed to the work), and suggestions for what to explore next. Concepts from past sessions come back later
   as spaced review.

## Learning moment types
| Type | Example (training a model) | When it fits |
|---|---|---|
| **Decide** | "Classes are 90/10 imbalanced. Accuracy or F1 as our metric, and why?" Claude then uses the choice. | A real fork in the work. Strongest for agency. |
| **Predict** | "Before I run this: what will happen to validation loss as we add epochs?" Result revealed after. | Right before a result appears |
| **Explain-back** | "In one sentence: why did we scale the features?" | Right after Claude did something new |
| **Spot the issue** | "This split has a subtle problem. Find it." (data leakage) | Code or config the user should be able to review |
| **Fill the gap** | "What value would you set for `test_size`?" | Small, low-risk parameters |

## Decided: work first, learning injected (2026-10-17)
Dinakar asked to weigh two models:
- **(A) Teach first, then work.** Upfront learning, with collaboration happening at boss level.
- **(B) Work first, inject learning.** The user starts working immediately; moments are inserted as concepts come up.

**Decision: (B), with micro-teaching inside each moment and milestone bosses as checkpoints.** Accepted by Dinakar.
- It matches the brief, which literally asks to "turn AI-assisted work into learning opportunities".
- Working professionals came to get something done. Front-loaded lessons delay value and feel like a detour, so they get skipped.
- Learning at the moment of need is more motivating and transfers better: the concept is immediately used on *their* problem.
- (A) survives in micro form: the 2–4 sentence concept card right before each question is "teach first", just at the scale of one concept.
- Risk: interruptions break flow. Mitigations are a quality bar for moments, optional guardrails, skip/defer ("quiz me at the end"), and never interrupting mid-stream.
- Where (A) is better: total novices who don't know what to ask. Mitigation: if the intent step reveals a novice, offer an opt-in 60-second primer.

## Pacing engine (code, per P8)
**Default: no limits.** Not every interaction is equally ripe for learning, so whenever a great learning moment presents
itself, we show it. No fixed budget or cooldown by default.

- Each Claude turn returns structured output: the work response, the concepts it touched, and an optional *candidate*
  learning moment (type, concept, question, rubric, multiple-choice fallback, ideal answer, and a **learning-value
  score** with a one-line justification).
- Since there's no budget by default, the **quality bar** is what keeps this from becoming spammy. Code shows a
  candidate when:
  - its learning-value score clears the threshold,
  - the concept isn't already mastered (stale concepts resurface as review),
  - it targets the user's challenge band (P5).
- **Optional guardrails (opt-in):** users who want fewer interruptions can enable guardrails in settings, then dial between:
  | Mode | Behavior (initial values, to tune) |
  |---|---|
  | Light | Soft cap ~1 moment per 2 turns; nothing else changes |
  | Balanced | ~3–5 moments per 10 min, ≥2 turns between moments |
  | Strict | ~1–2 moments per 10 min, only the highest-value moments; the rest deferred to the wrap-up quiz |
  Caps are soft: an exceptional moment (e.g., the user is about to make a costly mistake) may still break through.
  Strict = fewest interruptions (confirmed).
- **Timing:** decide and predict moments come *before* the related work is shown. For predict moments the work can be
  generated and held back; decide moments need a second call that uses the user's choice. Explain-back and
  spot-the-issue moments come *after*.
- **Grading:** Claude grades free-form answers against the rubric (correct / partial / incorrect + why). After one miss
  or a clear struggle, offer the multiple-choice version.
- **Future improvement:** tune the default (and the guardrail values) based on what works better for users; for
  example, track skip rates, answer rates, and session completion per mode.

## Rewards and look
- **Permanent XP bar and player level** across all sessions. Levels unlock visual themes and sound packs (settings behind the gear; P1).
- Story chapters as milestone rewards: surprise genre, lightly themed to the work.
- ASCII characters: guide reactions (Pip the robot), bosses (`reference/ascii-characters.md`).
- "Frost" theme (light blue / white / silver), Nunito font, Kenney CC0 sounds, minimal on-screen clutter.

## Real code execution (researched 2026-10-17, `reference/research/08-code-execution.md`)
- **Plan:** Claude actually runs code using Anthropic's **server-side code execution tool**: real Python + scikit-learn in
  an isolated, offline sandbox, with only the API key. Files persist across turns via a reused container, so the
  predict moments and bosses use *real* metrics and charts.
- **Not feasible for the prototype:** connecting the hosted site to a user's *local* Claude Code (a server can't reach a
  laptop), or hosting the Claude Agent SDK (needs a container per user; ~8–12 h, high risk).
- **Future improvement, "local mode":** a small local companion (e.g., `npx co-learn-bridge`) that dials out to Co-learn
  and lets learning moments run on the user's own Claude Code session, repo, and data.
- **Demo data:** a seeded **synthetic churn CSV** (~5,000 customers, ~15% churn) bundled with a one-click
  "try the demo" starter. It has no license issues, and the imbalance sets up a natural "accuracy is misleading" moment.
  Free-form tasks still work.
- **Fallback:** a pre-recorded real run, replayed and clearly labeled "replayed", if the sandbox fails during review.

## Follow-ups (not in the prototype)
- **Explicit topic learning:** a user says "I want to learn about US presidents" (a subject, not a task). The work-first design partly covers this today, since Claude's "work" becomes explaining and moments still fire. A dedicated mode would reuse the section/boss structure from `alternative-projects/learning-quest/`.

## Platform and model
Hosted web app. Next.js on Vercel. Claude via the Vercel AI SDK; Claude-only for now, model-agnostic as P1.
Opus 5.5 / Sonnet 5.5 / Haiku 5.5 routed by task. Per-turn execution (incl. code runs): **Sonnet 5.5** by default; switch to Opus 5.5 if Sonnet
stumbles on multi-step code during testing. Claude effort setting: **high** for planning calls (intent →
session plan, boss design), **medium** for per-turn execution calls.

## 14. Demo dataset (`web/scripts/generate_churn.py`, seeded)

**Size and balance:** 5,000 rows, ~15% churn.

**Columns:** `customer_id`, `tenure_months`, `contract_type` (month-to-month / one-year / two-year), `monthly_charges`,
`total_charges` (≈ tenure × monthly, with ~1% missing), `support_tickets_90d`, `payment_method`, `has_premium_support`,
`last_login_days_ago`, `plan_tier`, **`cancellation_request_date`** (planted leak: mostly filled for churners), `churned`.

**How churn is generated:** logistic in tenure, contract, tickets, and charges, plus noise.

**Teaching hooks this sets up:**
- Imbalance: accuracy is misleading.
- A leak to spot.
- Missing values to handle.
- Correlated features (total vs. monthly × tenure).

**Upload:** once, via the Files API, with the ID stored as `DEMO_FILE_ID`. It's attached as a container upload on the demo's first turn.

| Scale to millions | Stateless serverless routes; prompt caching; Haiku for cheap gates/grading; the pacing engine is deterministic code (no extra model cost); sandbox per session is Anthropic-managed; per-user state is small JSON |
| Sister-team adoption | The **`learning_moment` tool + pacing engine is a surface-agnostic contract**. # Product vision: Co-learn (v1, Option B)

Authored with Dinakar, 2026-10-17. The previous topic-to-game vision is archived in `alternative-projects/learning-quest/`.

## One-liner
**Co-learn is a mode for Claude where you get real work done *and* come out more capable.** Claude collaborates on
your task as usual, but at the right moments it turns the work into short, game-like challenges you solve yourself.
Your answers often steer the work.

## Framing
Imagined as a mode that ships inside Claude (e.g., `/co-learn` in Claude.ai or Claude Code). The prototype is a
standalone web app that emulates that mode on the Claude API.

## Target user and demo
- **User:** a working professional using Claude to get a task done in an area where they're not yet an expert, who wants to grow rather than just delegate.
- **Demo scenario (video):** training a machine-learning model, e.g., "help me train a model to predict customer churn from this CSV".
- **Session length:** 10 minutes by default.

## Experience
0. **Unlock.** The landing page is a single input whose placeholder shows `/co-learn` like a password hint. Typing it
   unlocks the site with a small animation and sound. It frames Co-learn as a mode you switch on. It is **not**
   security: the "password" is shown on screen, so abuse protection comes from rate limits.
1. **Intent.** At most 2–3 quick questions: what are you working on, how familiar are you with this area, and roughly
   how long you have (10 minutes by default). Learning guardrails are off by default (see Pacing).
2. **Work.** The user prompts and Claude works on the task, as in normal Claude.
3. **Learning moments.** Small, discrete challenges triggered by what the user is doing *right now*, not a pre-planned
   curriculum (the work changes too much as it goes). Each moment:
   - an optional 2–4 sentence concept card,
   - a free-form question,
   - a multiple-choice version if the user struggles,
   - a short "why" as feedback, plus XP and a sound,
   - then Claude continues the work, using the user's answer where it applies.
4. **Milestone bosses.** When a chunk of work completes (data prepared, first model trained), a short boss challenge
   recombines the concepts from recent moments, e.g., "Train accuracy is 99% and validation is 61%. What's happening, and what's the first thing you'd change?"
5. **Wrap-up.** A recap "codex" of concepts learned this session, XP and level progress, a story chapter (a surprise,
   lightly themed to the work), and suggestions for what to explore next. Concepts from past sessions come back later
   as spaced review.

## Learning moment types
| Type | Example (training a model) | When it fits |
|---|---|---|
| **Decide** | "Classes are 90/10 imbalanced. Accuracy or F1 as our metric, and why?" Claude then uses the choice. | A real fork in the work. Strongest for agency. |
| **Predict** | "Before I run this: what will happen to validation loss as we add epochs?" Result revealed after. | Right before a result appears |
| **Explain-back** | "In one sentence: why did we scale the features?" | Right after Claude did something new |
| **Spot the issue** | "This split has a subtle problem. Find it." (data leakage) | Code or config the user should be able to review |
| **Fill the gap** | "What value would you set for `test_size`?" | Small, low-risk parameters |

## Decided: work first, learning injected (2026-10-17)
Dinakar asked to weigh two models:
- **(A) Teach first, then work.** Upfront learning, with collaboration happening at boss level.
- **(B) Work first, inject learning.** The user starts working immediately; moments are inserted as concepts come up.

**Decision: (B), with micro-teaching inside each moment and milestone bosses as checkpoints.** Accepted by Dinakar.
- It matches the brief, which literally asks to "turn AI-assisted work into learning opportunities".
- Working professionals came to get something done. Front-loaded lessons delay value and feel like a detour, so they get skipped.
- Learning at the moment of need is more motivating and transfers better: the concept is immediately used on *their* problem.
- (A) survives in micro form: the 2–4 sentence concept card right before each question is "teach first", just at the scale of one concept.
- Risk: interruptions break flow. Mitigations are a quality bar for moments, optional guardrails, skip/defer ("quiz me at the end"), and never interrupting mid-stream.
- Where (A) is better: total novices who don't know what to ask. Mitigation: if the intent step reveals a novice, offer an opt-in 60-second primer.

## Pacing engine (code, per P8)
**Default: no limits.** Not every interaction is equally ripe for learning, so whenever a great learning moment presents
itself, we show it. No fixed budget or cooldown by default.

- Each Claude turn returns structured output: the work response, the concepts it touched, and an optional *candidate*
  learning moment (type, concept, question, rubric, multiple-choice fallback, ideal answer, and a **learning-value
  score** with a one-line justification).
- Since there's no budget by default, the **quality bar** is what keeps this from becoming spammy. Code shows a
  candidate when:
  - its learning-value score clears the threshold,
  - the concept isn't already mastered (stale concepts resurface as review),
  - it targets the user's challenge band (P5).
- **Optional guardrails (opt-in):** users who want fewer interruptions can enable guardrails in settings, then dial between:
  | Mode | Behavior (initial values, to tune) |
  |---|---|
  | Light | Soft cap ~1 moment per 2 turns; nothing else changes |
  | Balanced | ~3–5 moments per 10 min, ≥2 turns between moments |
  | Strict | ~1–2 moments per 10 min, only the highest-value moments; the rest deferred to the wrap-up quiz |
  Caps are soft: an exceptional moment (e.g., the user is about to make a costly mistake) may still break through.
  Strict = fewest interruptions (confirmed).
- **Timing:** decide and predict moments come *before* the related work is shown. For predict moments the work can be
  generated and held back; decide moments need a second call that uses the user's choice. Explain-back and
  spot-the-issue moments come *after*.
- **Grading:** Claude grades free-form answers against the rubric (correct / partial / incorrect + why). After one miss
  or a clear struggle, offer the multiple-choice version.
- **Future improvement:** tune the default (and the guardrail values) based on what works better for users; for
  example, track skip rates, answer rates, and session completion per mode.

## Rewards and look
- **Permanent XP bar and player level** across all sessions. Levels unlock visual themes and sound packs (settings behind the gear; P1).
- Story chapters as milestone rewards: surprise genre, lightly themed to the work.
- ASCII characters: guide reactions (Pip the robot), bosses (`reference/ascii-characters.md`).
- "Frost" theme (light blue / white / silver), Nunito font, Kenney CC0 sounds, minimal on-screen clutter.

## Real code execution (researched 2026-10-17, `reference/research/08-code-execution.md`)
- **Plan:** Claude actually runs code using Anthropic's **server-side code execution tool**: real Python + scikit-learn in
  an isolated, offline sandbox, with only the API key. Files persist across turns via a reused container, so the
  predict moments and bosses use *real* metrics and charts.
- **Not feasible for the prototype:** connecting the hosted site to a user's *local* Claude Code (a server can't reach a
  laptop), or hosting the Claude Agent SDK (needs a container per user; ~8–12 h, high risk).
- **Future improvement, "local mode":** a small local companion (e.g., `npx co-learn-bridge`) that dials out to Co-learn
  and lets learning moments run on the user's own Claude Code session, repo, and data.
- **Demo data:** a seeded **synthetic churn CSV** (~5,000 customers, ~15% churn) bundled with a one-click
  "try the demo" starter. It has no license issues, and the imbalance sets up a natural "accuracy is misleading" moment.
  Free-form tasks still work.
- **Fallback:** a pre-recorded real run, replayed and clearly labeled "replayed", if the sandbox fails during review.

## Follow-ups (not in the prototype)
- **Explicit topic learning:** a user says "I want to learn about US presidents" (a subject, not a task). The work-first design partly covers this today, since Claude's "work" becomes explaining and moments still fire. A dedicated mode would reuse the section/boss structure from `alternative-projects/learning-quest/`.

## Platform and model
Hosted web app. Next.js on Vercel. Claude via the Vercel AI SDK; Claude-only for now, model-agnostic as P1.
Opus 5.5 / Sonnet 5.5 / Haiku 5.5 routed by task. Per-turn execution (incl. code runs): **Sonnet 5.5** by default; switch to Opus 5.5 if Sonnet
stumbles on multi-step code during testing. Claude effort setting: **high** for planning calls (intent →
session plan, boss design), **medium** for per-turn execution calls.

# Building LLM-Powered Applications with Claude

This skill helps you build LLM-powered applications with Claude. Choose the right surface based on your needs, detect the project language, then read the relevant language-specific documentation.

## Before You Start

Scan the target file (or, if no target file, the prompt and project) for non-Anthropic provider markers - `import openai`, `from openai`, `langchain_openai`, `OpenAI(`, `gpt-4`, `gpt-5`, file names like `agent-openai.py` or `*-generic.py`, or any explicit instruction to keep the code provider-neutral. If you find any, stop and tell the user that this skill produces Claude/Anthropic SDK code; ask whether they want to switch the file to Claude or want a non-Claude implementation. Do not edit a non-Anthropic file with Anthropic SDK calls. (Exception: the `prompt-audit` subcommand is non-interactive and does not stop here - it records non-Anthropic provider markers in its report's stated assumptions and never proposes switching a non-Anthropic file to the Anthropic SDK.)

## Output Requirement

When the user asks you to add, modify, or implement a Claude feature, your code must call Claude through one of:

1. **The official Anthropic SDK** for the project's language (`anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, `com.anthropic.*`, etc.). This is the default whenever a supported SDK exists for the project.
2. **Raw HTTP** (`curl`, `requests`, `fetch`, `httpx`, etc.) - only when the user explicitly asks for cURL/REST/raw HTTP, the project is a shell/cURL project, or the language has no official SDK.

Never mix the two - don't reach for `requests`/`fetch` in a Python or TypeScript project just because it feels lighter. Never fall back to OpenAI-compatible shims.

**Never guess SDK usage.** Function names, class names, namespaces, method signatures, and import paths must come from explicit documentation - either the `{lang}/` files in this skill or the official SDK repositories or documentation links listed in `shared/live-sources.md`. If the binding you need is not explicitly documented in the skill files, WebFetch the relevant SDK repo from `shared/live-sources.md` before writing code. Do not infer Ruby/Java/Go/PHP/C# APIs from cURL shapes or from another language's SDK.

**If WebFetch or repository access fails** (network restricted, timeouts, clone blocked): do not keep retrying - write code from the patterns and namespace/package tables in the `{lang}/` file, run the compiler or interpreter on it, and iterate on the error output. For statically-typed SDKs (C#, Java, Go) a compile-fix loop against local errors reaches working code faster than blocked network research.

## Defaults

Unless the user requests otherwise:

For the Claude model version, please use Claude Opus 5.5, which you can access via the exact model string `claude-opus-5-5`. Please default to using adaptive thinking (`thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`) for anything remotely complicated. And finally, please default to streaming for any request that may involve long input, long output, or high `max_tokens` - it prevents hitting request timeouts. Use the SDK's `.get_final_message()` / `.finalMessage()` helper to get the complete response if you don't need to handle individual stream events. When a streaming request defines user-defined (client) tools, set `eager_input_streaming: true` on each of those tools so large tool inputs (file contents, code, documents) stream as they are generated instead of arriving in one burst after the server finishes buffering them; the client then owns validation: the SDKs' tolerant parsers can return a silently truncated input instead of raising, so validate each parsed tool input against its schema before running it (the typed runner helpers such as `betaZodTool` / typed `@beta_tool` do this; `betaTool()` JSON-Schema tools and manual loops must validate themselves), treat a failure like invalid JSON (`INVALID_JSON` error `tool_result` when you hold the block, re-issue otherwise), check `max_tokens` / `refusal` stop reasons before running tools, and catch only the SDK's JSON error, never its typed API errors - pattern in `shared/tool-use-concepts.md` -> Eager input streaming. Leave it off for non-streaming requests, for server tools, and when the request goes through a proxy or an older Bedrock model deployment that rejects the field.

## Warning: API Drift - Your Training Prior May Be Stale

Several common Claude API shapes changed in 2025-2026. If you recall a pattern from training, verify it against the `{lang}/` files in this skill before writing - the rows below are the most frequent drift points:

| Area | Stale prior | Current API |
|---|---|---|
| Extended thinking | `thinking: {type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N}` | On Claude 4.6+ models: `thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`. `budget_tokens` is deprecated on Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6 and **rejected with a 400** on Fable 5/5.1 / Sonnet 5.5 / Sonnet 5 / Opus 5.5 / 5 / 4.8 / 4.7. Pre-4.6 models still use `budget_tokens`. |
| Web search / web fetch tool type | `web_search_20250305`, `web_fetch_20250910` | `web_search_20260209`, `web_fetch_20260209` (dynamic filtering) on Opus 5.5/5/4.8/4.7/4.6, Sonnet 5.5, Sonnet 5, and Sonnet 4.6. Older models keep the basic variants; on Vertex AI only basic `web_search_20250305` is available (web fetch is not on Vertex) - see the Server Tools QR below. |
| PHP parameter names | snake_case wire names as named args (`max_tokens`) | Top-level named args are camelCase (`maxTokens`). Nested array keys vary by feature (e.g. `'taskBudget'`, `'skillID'`, `'mcp_server_name'`) - copy the exact key from the documented example; do not bulk-convert. |
| Managed Agents credentials | Keep secrets host-side via custom tools (the only option before vaults shipped) | Vault `environment_variable` credentials - stored by Anthropic, substituted at egress, never visible in the sandbox (`shared/managed-agents-tools.md` -> Vaults). Host-side custom tools remain the fallback for self-hosted sandboxes. |
| Files API / Skills | `client.beta.files.*` / `client.beta.skills.*` with beta `files-api-2025-04-14` / `skills-2025-10-02` | Out of beta: `client.files.*` / `client.skills.*`, no beta header. In current SDKs `client.beta.files` / `client.beta.skills` have breaking shape changes from previous versions, matching the stable namespaces - migrate per `shared/live-sources.md` -> Files API / Skills Guide. |

The `{lang}/` files in this skill are authoritative over recalled patterns.

---

## Subcommands

## Which Surface Should I Use?

> **Start simple.** Default to the simplest tier that meets your needs. Single API calls and workflows handle most use cases - only reach for agents when the task genuinely requires open-ended, model-driven exploration. "Simplest" means the least code you own: for a hosted, scheduled, or memory-backed agent, Managed Agents is usually the simplest option (no loop code, no state files, no scheduler), even though it's a bigger platform.

| Use Case                                        | Tier            | Recommended Surface       | Why                                                          |
| ----------------------------------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Classification, summarization, extraction, Q&A  | Single LLM call | **Claude API**            | One request, one response                                    |
| Batch processing or embeddings                  | Single LLM call | **Claude API**            | Specialized endpoints                                        |
| Multi-step pipelines with code-controlled logic | Workflow        | **Claude API + tool use** | You orchestrate the loop                                     |
| Custom agent with your own tools                | Agent           | **Claude API + tool use** | Maximum flexibility                                          |
| Server-managed stateful agent with workspace    | Agent           | **Managed Agents**        | Anthropic runs the loop and hosts the tool-execution sandbox |
| Persisted, versioned agent configs              | Agent           | **Managed Agents**        | Agents are stored objects; sessions pin to a version         |
| Long-running multi-turn agent with file mounts  | Agent           | **Managed Agents**        | Per-session containers, SSE event stream, Skills + MCP       |
| Agent that runs on a schedule (cron, "every night") | Agent       | **Managed Agents** - scheduled deployments | Deployments fire sessions autonomously; no client-side scheduler |
| One deliverable that must meet a quality bar ("until it's right") | Agent | **Managed Agents** - outcomes | A separate grader iterates the agent against your rubric until it passes |
| Agent work too big to hand out one task at a time | Agent | **Managed Agents** - dynamic workflows | Many agents in phases |

> **Note:** Managed Agents is the right choice when you want Anthropic to run the agent loop *and* host the container where tools execute - file ops, bash, code execution all run in the per-session workspace. If you want to host the compute yourself or run your own custom tool runtime, Claude API + tool use is the right choice - use the tool runner for the agentic loop - its per-turn hooks still give you approval gates, logging, error interception, and conditional execution (see `shared/tool-use-concepts.md`) - or the manual loop when you want to own the entire loop yourself.

> **Cloud-provider access.** **Claude Platform on AWS** is Anthropic-operated with same-day API parity - see `shared/claude-platform-on-aws.md` for client setup. For per-feature availability on **Claude Platform on AWS**, **Amazon Bedrock**, **Google Vertex AI**, and **Microsoft Foundry**, see `shared/platform-availability.md` - that table is the single source of truth in this skill; do not infer availability from anywhere else.

### Building an Agent: Four Approaches

Once you've decided you actually need an agent (open-ended, model-driven tool use), there are four distinct ways to build one. Two independent questions separate them: **who supplies the harness** (the agent loop + context management) and **who supplies the deployment** (the infra the agent runs on). The Tool Runner and the Claude Agent SDK both supply a *harness only* - you still host and deploy them yourself - which is why they're easy to conflate. Managed Agents (CMA) is the only option that supplies **both** the harness *and* managed deployment; the manual loop supplies neither.

| # | Approach | You write | Harness & deployment | Tools available | Use when |
|---|----------|-----------|----------------------|-----------------|----------|
| 1 | **Claude API - manual loop** | The `while stop_reason == "tool_use"` loop yourself | You build the harness; you host | Only tools you define | You want to own the *entire* loop - no beta dependency, or a control flow the Tool Runner's per-turn hooks don't fit |
| 2 | **Claude API - Tool Runner** (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner` + `@beta_tool` / `betaZodTool`) | Just the tool functions | SDK supplies the loop (**harness only**); you host | Only tools you define | A custom-tool agent without hand-writing the loop (most cases). Per-turn hooks still give you approval gates, error interception, result modification (e.g. `cache_control`), retries, streaming, and compaction |
| 3 | **Managed Agents** (REST, beta) | Agent config + your tool results | Anthropic supplies the harness **and** hosts a per-session sandbox (**harness + deployment**) | Anthropic-hosted sandbox (bash, files, code exec) + Skills/MCP + your tools | You want Anthropic to run the loop *and* host the per-session workspace; persisted/versioned configs; long-running sessions |
| 4 | **Claude Agent SDK** - *separate product* (`claude-agent-sdk` / `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`) | A prompt + options | SDK supplies the Claude Code harness + built-in tools (**harness only**); you host | Built-in Read/Write/Edit/Bash/Glob/Grep/WebSearch/WebFetch + MCP + subagents | You want a batteries-included coding/filesystem agent running on your own infra |

The harness/deployment split is the key mental model: options 1, 2, and 4 all **leave deployment to you**; only option 3 (CMA) adds managed deployment. Options 1-3 are what this skill generates; option 4 is a different library with its own docs - see the disambiguation below.

> **Tool Runner != Claude Agent SDK.** These sound alike but are different packages:
> - **Tool Runner** is part of the regular Anthropic API SDK (`anthropic` / `@anthropic-ai/sdk`), reached via `client.beta.messages.tool_runner`. It automates the request -> execute -> loop cycle *for tools you define*. No built-in tools, no filesystem access, no sandbox - you supply every tool and host the compute. It is option 2 above, a thin helper over `POST /v1/messages`.
> - **Claude Agent SDK** (`claude-agent-sdk` / `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`) is Claude Code packaged as a library. It ships built-in tools (file read/write/edit, bash, grep, web search), the full agent loop, context management, hooks, subagents, permissions, and sessions. You call `query(prompt, options)` and it drives everything.
>
> Both are **harness-only - you host and deploy them.** The difference is scope of harness: the Tool Runner loops over tools *you* define (with per-turn hooks for approval, interception, result modification, and retries - but no built-in tools); the Agent SDK is the full Claude Code harness with built-in tools. Neither provides managed deployment - that's what **Managed Agents (CMA)** adds (Anthropic hosts the loop and a per-session sandbox).
>
> **This skill covers the Claude API and Managed Agents (options 1-3); it does not generate Claude Agent SDK code.** If the user actually wants the Claude Agent SDK, point them to its docs (`code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk`) - don't substitute the API Tool Runner for it, or vice-versa.

### Should I Build an Agent?

Before choosing the agent tier, check all four criteria:

- **Complexity** - Is the task multi-step and hard to fully specify in advance? (e.g., "turn this design doc into a PR" vs. "extract the title from this PDF")
- **Value** - Does the outcome justify higher cost and latency?
- **Viability** - Is Claude capable at this task type?
- **Cost of error** - Can errors be caught and recovered from? (tests, review, rollback)

If the answer is "no" to any of these, stay at a simpler tier (single call or workflow).

## Architecture

Everything goes through `POST /v1/messages`. Tools and output constraints are features of this single endpoint - not separate APIs.

**User-defined tools** - You define tools (via decorators, Zod schemas, or raw JSON), and the SDK's tool runner handles calling the API, executing your functions, and looping until Claude is done. For full control, you can write the loop manually.

**Server-side tools** - Anthropic-hosted tools that run on Anthropic's infrastructure. Code execution is fully server-side (declare it in `tools`, Claude runs code automatically). Computer use can be server-hosted or self-hosted.

**Structured outputs** - Constrains the Messages API response format (`output_config.format`) and/or tool parameter validation (`strict: true`). The recommended approach is `client.messages.parse()` which validates responses against your schema automatically. Note: the old `output_format` parameter is deprecated; use `output_config: {format: {...}}` on `messages.create()`.

**Supporting endpoints** - Batches (`POST /v1/messages/batches`), Files (`POST /v1/files`), Token Counting (`POST /v1/messages/count_tokens` - see `shared/token-counting.md`), and Models (`GET /v1/models`, `GET /v1/models/{id}` - live capability/context-window discovery) feed into or support Messages API requests.
